subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply button/select clicks remain heartbeat-owned system events, or should Slack synthesize normal inbound reply turns for user-initiated controls?
rationale: Current source proves the path is still heartbeat-owned, but changing it would replace a recently accepted Slack system-event design and must preserve plugin interactive handlers, native approvals, thread routing, and the separate session-conflict recovery work.

options.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
options.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with regression and live proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and active-run behavior.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat And Harden It
options.body: Retain the system-event heartbeat design, but require end-to-end proof that clicked values, visible replies, and retry behavior are reliable.

options.title: Defer To Shared Conflict Work
options.body: Wait for the general session-init conflict decision, then retest Slack interactions against that chosen recovery layer before changing the delivery owner.

recommendation.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
recommendation.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with regression and live proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and active-run behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the core system-event drain path and the prior closure that separated value surfacing from the remaining delivery-owner question.
